new.title: Climb into the Romanesque St. Patrokli-Dom
new.desc: The Patroklidom is Soest's Romanesque landmark, built from local green sandstone from the 12th century. Its 80-metre west tower is the symbol of the old town.
new.tip: Free entry during the day; the tower is only opened on special occasions.

new.title: Find the Westphalian Last Supper in the Wiesenkirche
new.desc: St. Maria zur Wiese is a High Gothic hall church begun in 1313. A window of about 1500 shows the Last Supper with ham, pumpernickel and beer, known as the Westphalian Last Supper.
new.tip: The church is under reconstruction work in parts; check what is open before you go.

new.title: Walk through the Osthofentor, Soest's last gate
new.desc: The Osthofentor is the only surviving gate fortress of the ten that once guarded Soest. It dates from the 14th and 15th centuries and now houses a small museum.
new.tip: Combine it with a walk on the old city wall promenade nearby.

new.title: Visit Alt-St. Petri, Soest's oldest church
new.desc: Alt-St. Petri is the oldest parish church of Soest, a Romanesque basilica of green sandstone near the market square.
new.tip: Check opening hours with the parish; guided tours run at times.

new.title: See the Gothic wall paintings of the Hohnekirche
new.desc: St. Maria zur Höhe, the Hohnekirche, is a Romanesque church with Gothic wall paintings and a notable altarpiece at the north of the old town.
new.tip: Check opening hours; it is often open on summer afternoons.

new.title: Explore the Burghofmuseum and Soest's history
new.desc: The Burghofmuseum shows the history of the Hanseatic town Soest, from its salt trade to the Soester Fehde of 1444-49.
new.tip: Closed Mondays; allow about an hour.

new.title: Step into the small Nikolaikapelle
new.desc: The Nikolaikapelle is a small Romanesque chapel by the Patrokli church, known for its medieval wall painting and its role in Soest's art history.
new.tip: Check opening hours; often visited together with the Patrokli-Dom.

new.title: Stroll to the Soester Rathaus and the Markt
new.desc: The Rathaus stands in the middle of the old town, framed by half-timbered houses and green sandstone walls.
new.tip: Pick up a free town map at the tourist information next door.

new.title: Walk the old Wallpromenade around Soest
new.desc: The medieval town wall of Soest, built from local green sandstone, is lined by a promenade of about 3.5 km, among the best preserved in Westphalia.
new.tip: Takes about an hour; start at the Osthofentor.

new.title: Stroll around the Großer Teich in Soest
new.desc: The Großer Teich lies just outside the old town walls, a quiet pond with walking paths and green space.
new.tip: Easy loop of about 30 minutes in good weather.

new.title: Join the Allerheiligenkirmes in the old town
new.desc: Soest's Allerheiligenkirmes is called Europe's largest old-town fair; it starts on the Wednesday after All Saints for five days, with rides and the mocha liqueur Bullenauge.
new.tip: Expect crowds; try a Bullenauge shot and bring cash.

new.title: Dine at the Pilgrimhaus, Westphalia's oldest inn
new.desc: The Pilgrimhaus on Jakobistraße calls itself the oldest inn in Westphalia. It serves Westphalian dishes and sells its own Soester Pumpernickel.
new.tip: Reserve for evenings; ask for Westphalian specialties.

new.title: Buy Soester Pumpernickel at Bäckerei Haverland
new.desc: Haverland is a bakery on the Marktplatz that claims to be the oldest pumpernickel bakery in the world, run by the same family since 1570.
new.tip: Try a pumpernickel with ham or take a loaf home.

new.title: Drink house beer at Brauerei Zwiebel
new.desc: Brauerei Zwiebel is a Soest brewpub serving house-brewed beer and Westphalian food.
new.tip: Order the house beer with a hearty plate.

new.title: Walk across the Möhnetalsperre dam
new.desc: The Möhne dam, completed in 1913, was breached in the Dambusters raid of 1943 and rebuilt. It holds back the Möhnesee.
new.tip: Walk along the crest for views of lake and valley.

new.title: See the Glockenturm in Arnsberg's old town
new.desc: The Glockenturm is the landmark of Arnsberg, a baroque tower on the old town hill, near the Maximilian Fountain.
new.tip: Walk up to the Schlossberg for views over the Ruhr bend.

new.title: Visit Kloster Oelinghausen near Arnsberg
new.desc: Kloster Oelinghausen is a former Premonstratensian convent from the 12th century with a Romanesque-Gothic church.
new.tip: Quiet valley setting; check the church opening hours.

new.title: Climb to Kloster Grafschaft above Schmallenberg
new.desc: The Benedictine Kloster Grafschaft sits on the hill above Schmallenberg, founded in 1072, with a baroque church.
new.tip: Open to visitors; the shop sells monastery goods.

new.title: Climb the Astenturm on the Kahler Asten
new.desc: The Kahler Asten (841 m) is one of the highest peaks of the Rothaar range. The Astenturm stands on its summit.
new.tip: Go on a clear day; the tower has an entry fee.

new.title: Hike to the Bruchhauser Steine rocks
new.desc: Four rock formations on the Istenberg near Olsberg, up to 92 m high, with remains of an Iron Age ring wall; a National Natural Monument.
new.tip: A fee supports the foundation; the marked loop takes about 2 hours.

new.title: Explore the hill town of Obermarsberg
new.desc: Obermarsberg is the site of the Saxon Eresburg, with the Stiftskirche St. Peter und Paul and a Roland statue above the Diemel valley.
new.tip: Combine with a walk along the Diemel valley.

new.title: Visit the Benedictine Abtei Königsmünster
new.desc: Abtei Königsmünster above Meschede was founded in 1928 and has a modern church and a monastery shop.
new.tip: Join a prayer service; tours by arrangement.

new.title: Find the Marienkirche in Lippstadt's old town
new.desc: The Marienkirche in Lippstadt is a Romanesque hall church with a Gothic choir in the old town.
new.tip: Free; combine with a stroll along the Lippe.

new.title: Tour Schloss Homburg in Nümbrecht
new.desc: Schloss Homburg is a medieval hilltop castle in Nümbrecht, now Museum und Forum with changing exhibitions.
new.tip: Check the current exhibition and opening days.

new.title: Step into the Tropfsteinhöhle Wiehl
new.desc: The Tropfsteinhöhle Wiehl, discovered in 1860, is a show cave with stalactites and a guided route.
new.tip: Guided tours; take a jacket as it is cool inside.

new.title: Wander the LVR Freilichtmuseum Lindlar
new.desc: The LVR-Freilichtmuseum in Lindlar presents historic Bergisch houses, crafts and farms, with seasonal events.
new.tip: Open from spring to autumn; check dates.

new.title: Walk the old town of Bergneustadt
new.desc: Bergneustadt is a small old town with a Burgplatz, half-timbered houses and the remains of the Schloss Neustadt.
new.tip: Compact old town; the Fachwerk lanes are best.

new.title: Eat regional cooking at Gasthof Schütte
new.desc: The Landhotel Gasthof Schütte in Schmallenberg is a family-run inn with regional and classic cuisine and an open fireplace in winter.
new.tip: Reserve for dinner; ask for the Sauerland dish of the day.

new.title: Dine at the Gasthof zur Post in Neuastenberg
new.desc: A family-run inn since 1850 in Neuastenberg near Winterberg, serving Sauerland dishes.
new.tip: Combine with a hike on the Kahler Asten.

new.title: Eat currywurst at the Hoheleyer Hütte
new.desc: The Hoheleyer Hütte is a hiking hut on several trails near Winterberg, serving pea soup, schnitzel and bratwurst.
new.tip: Listed open daily 11-19; check seasonal changes.

new.title: Drink house-brewed beer at Arnsberger Mühlenbräu
new.desc: A Gasthausbrauerei in Arnsberg's old town with house beer and organic, vegetarian and vegan dishes.
new.tip: Try the house lager.

new.title: Taste craft beer at Brauhaus Thombansen in Lippstadt
new.desc: A Lippstadt brewpub known for fresh tank beer and a varied menu.
new.tip: Reserve at weekends.

new.title: Dine at the Almer Schlossmühle near Brilon
new.desc: A restaurant in the Almer Schlossmühle in Brilon, with mains around 22 to 45 euros.
new.tip: Book ahead.

new.title: Order a coffee table at Landgasthof Tönnes in Wipperfürth
new.desc: Landgasthof Tönnes in Wipperfürth is a country inn in the Bergisches Land offering the Bergische Kaffeetafel.
new.tip: Reserve for groups.

new.title: Eat at the half-timbered Hohkeppeler Hof in Lindlar
new.desc: A Fachwerk house from 1784/85, now a restaurant with beer garden in Lindlar.
new.tip: Good after the Freilichtmuseum.

new.title: Eat at Friedchen's Gasthof in Warstein
new.desc: A Gasthof in Warstein recommended in local guides for regional cooking.
new.tip: Combine with the Warsteiner brewery visit.

new.title: Eat on the terrace at Gasthof Braun in Ohlenbach
new.desc: A family-run Gasthof between Winterberg and Schmallenberg with beer garden and rooms.
new.tip: Good rest stop between Winterberg and Schmallenberg.

new.title: Tour the Warsteiner Brauerei visitor centre
new.desc: The Warsteiner brewery offers a 360-degree film and a tour of the Waldpark brewery grounds by train, with a tasting.
new.tip: Registration needed; hours vary, check with the brewery.
new.q: Warsteiner Brauerei Besucherzentrum, Zu Hause im Waldpark 10, Warstein

new.title: Visit the Veltins brewery in Grevenstein
new.desc: The Brauerei C. & A. Veltins in Meschede-Grevenstein is a family brewery with its own beer garden.
new.tip: Check the brewery website for tour dates.
new.q: Brauerei C. & A. Veltins, An der Streue, Meschede-Grevenstein

new.title: Ride the Sommerrodelbahn at Erlebnisberg Kappe
new.desc: The Kappe summer toboggan run in Winterberg is about 700 m long, with bridges, curves and a controllable sled.
new.tip: Check the weather; a lift takes you up.

new.title: Ski the Skiliftkarussell in Winterberg
new.desc: The Skiliftkarussell is one of the largest ski areas in the region, with many lifts and slopes around Winterberg.
new.tip: Winter only; buy a day pass at the valley station.

new.title: Hike the Rothaarsteig from the Kahler Asten
new.desc: The Rothaarsteig long-distance trail passes the Kahler Asten, offering forest and moorland walks.
new.tip: Start at the Asten car park.

new.title: Cruise the Möhnesee on an electric boat
new.desc: Möhneseeschifffahrt runs electric excursion boats on the Möhnesee.
new.tip: Check the timetable by season.

new.title: Ride the MS Sorpesee on the Sorpe reservoir
new.desc: The MS Sorpesee ship offers tours on the Sorpesee near Sundern.
new.tip: Check the timetable by season.

new.title: Sail the Hennesee on the EMS Hennesee
new.desc: EMS Hennesee Boat Tours operates boats on the Hennesee near Meschede.
new.tip: Check the timetable by season.

new.title: Spend a day at Fort Fun Abenteuerland
new.desc: Fort Fun in Bestwig is a Wild-West-themed park; the 2025 season ran from 12 April to 2 November.
new.tip: Check dates for each season.

new.title: Walk the treetop path at Panarbora in Waldbröl
new.desc: Panarbora is a nature park with a treetop walkway and wilderness experiences in Waldbröl.
new.tip: Check seasonal opening times.

new.title: Descend into the Aggertalhöhle in Engelskirchen
new.desc: The Aggertalhöhle is a limestone cave in Engelskirchen, open for guided tours.
new.tip: Check opening dates; it is cool inside.

new.title: Explore the Westfälische Salzwelten in Bad Sassendorf
new.desc: Bad Sassendorf has a long salt history, shown in the Westfälische Salzwelten, with saline and brine baths nearby.
new.tip: Combine with a walk in the Kurpark.
